title: Propose a caching strategy for a read-heavy product catalog service
description: A read-heavy 'product catalog' service currently hits the database on every request and is becoming a bottleneck. Produce a caching strategy proposal covering cache placement (in-process vs. shared), invalidation strategy on writes, staleness tolerance, and cold-start/thundering-herd handling, plus a minimal interface skeleton for the chosen caching abstraction.
acceptanceCriteria: The proposal explicitly justifies a cache placement choice given the service's stated read/write ratio and multi-instance deployment.
The proposal defines a concrete invalidation strategy triggered by writes, not a fixed-TTL-only approach, unless a fixed TTL is explicitly justified as sufficient given stated staleness tolerance.
The proposal addresses thundering-herd risk on cache misses for popular keys (e.g. request coalescing or a stale-while-revalidate approach).
A minimal interface skeleton for the caching abstraction is provided and compiles, decoupled from any specific cache backend.
The proposal states measurable success criteria (e.g. target cache hit rate, target p95 latency) rather than only qualitative goals.
verificationMethod: architecture-check (human-review as primary authority): reviewed against the acceptance criteria; interface skeleton verified to compile.
groundTruth: A sound proposal uses a shared cache (given multi-instance deployment) with write-triggered invalidation (or explicit versioned keys), request coalescing (a single in-flight fetch per key on miss) to prevent thundering herd, and a backend-agnostic Cache interface (get/set/invalidate) so the backend can change without touching call sites.
